headline: Probing and auditing what biological sequence foundation models actually encode
label: Foundation Models For Biological Sequences
summary: Pre-registered and contamination-aware evaluations now test whether DNA, RNA, and single-cell foundation models outperform strong controls.
synthesis: The dominant thread is interrogation of learned representations rather than headline benchmark performance. Sparse autoencoders on Nucleotide Transformer and DNABERT-2 recover transcription-factor motif features, and causal ablation with composition-matched validation identifies CTCF among them. Evo 2 embeddings decode viral genome architecture beyond 6-mer composition, and a training-free layer analysis indicates that representative and load-bearing layers dissociate, with mid-layer pooling beating last-layer pooling on ClinVar variants. On the data side, scContam combines MinHash gene-set fingerprinting with loss-based membership inference to audit pretraining contamination in single-cell models, and Shifu pairs a leakage-audited 254k-sequence RNA structure corpus with multi-axis evaluation. Pre-registered external evaluation of Geneformer, scGPT, and UCE on Replogle Perturb-seq finds that all beat controls, yet none reliably beats a strong baseline. What is new is the emphasis on falsifiable evaluation design. A nasal microbiome index and a microbiome foundation model sit at the periphery of this thread.
